subject_line: A poem written into a microbe, and now Darwin
email_body:
Dear Christian,

The idea at the heart of The Xenotext, writing a poem into the genome of a microbe so that the organism itself answers with a poem of its own, remains one of poetry's boldest experiments. Now that you teach in Darwin, I wondered whether working in the Top End, far from the Canadian scene where Eunoia was written, has changed how you think about constraint and about where a poem can live.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Experimental poet (Eunoia; The Xenotext project encoding a poem in bacterial DNA) now lecturing in literary studies at Charles Darwin University; email seen in search result on CDU supervisor page.
